label: pro: relatively free algebra
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro: relatively free algebra}
Let $W\langle x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-\rangle $ be the free $(W,*)$-algebra in $n$ symmetric variables and $n$ skew-symmetric variables, and  $$\psi\colon W\langle x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-\rangle \to H$$
be the $(W,*)$-homomorphism induced by $\psi(x_i^+)=\xi_i^+$ and $\psi(x_i^-)=\xi_i^-$, $1\leq i \leq n$. Then 
$$
\ker\psi=\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(A)\cap W\langle x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-\rangle.
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We start by proving that $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(A)\cap W\langle x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-\rangle \subseteq \ker\psi.$ To this end, let $f=f(x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-) \in
     W\langle x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-\rangle$ be a $(W,*)$-identity of $A$.
    Since the field $F$ is of characteristic zero, we can assume that $f$ is a multilinear $(W,*)$-polynomial. Then, by \eqref{eq: generic elem}, $ \psi(f)=f(\xi_1^+, \ldots, \xi_n^+,\xi_1^-,\ldots , \xi_n^-)$ is a sum of the expressions of the form
    $$\bar{f}=f(\xi_{1,j_1} \otimes a_{j_1}, \ldots , \xi_{n,j_n} \otimes a_{j_n}, \xi_{1,l_1} \otimes b_{l_1}, \ldots , \xi_{n,l_n} \otimes b_{l_n})= \xi_{1,p_1} \cdots \xi_{n,p_n} \otimes f(  a_{j_1}, \ldots ,  a_{j_n},  b_{l_1}, \ldots ,  b_{l_n}),$$
    where $p_i\in \{j_i,l_i\}$ for $1\leq i \le n$. Since $f\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(A)$, we get that $\bar{f}=0$, and as a consequence $f\in \ker \psi$, as required.

    Suppose now that $f(x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-)\in \ker \psi$, i.e., $f(\xi_{1}^+, \ldots,\xi_{n}^+, \xi_{1}^-,\ldots, \xi_{n}^-)=0 $ in $H$, and let $c_1,\ldots, c_n$ be arbitrary symmetric elements of  $A$ and $d_1,\ldots, d_n$ be arbitrary skew-symmetric elements of  $A$. Write each $c_i$ as a linear combination of the basis $\mathcal{B}^+$ of $A^+$ and $d_i$ as a linear combination of the basis $\mathcal{B}^-$ of $A^-$. Then, for $1\leq i \leq n$, there exist $\alpha_{i,1}, \ldots, \alpha_{i,s}, \beta_{i,s+1},\ldots,\beta_{i,s+t}\in F$ such that
    $$
    c_i=\sum_{j=1}^s \alpha_{i,j}a_{j} \quad \text{and} \quad d_i=\sum_{j=1}^t \beta_{i,s+j}b_{j}.
    $$
    By the universal property of the free commutative algebra $F[\xi_{i,j}]$ and of the tensor product, we can consider the $(W,*)$-homomorphism $\rho: F[\xi_{i,j}] \otimes A \to A$ which restricts to the identity on $A$ and, for each $1\leq i \leq n$, satisfies
$$\rho(\xi_{i,j})=\begin{cases}
    \alpha_{i,j}, & \text{if }1\leq j \leq s\\
    \beta_{i,j}, & \text{if }s+1\leq j \leq s+t
\end{cases}.$$
Since $\rho(\xi_i^+)=c_i$ and $\rho(\xi_i^-)=d_i$, $1\leq i \leq n$, we obtain
$$0=\rho(f(\xi_{1}^+, \ldots,\xi_{n}^+, \xi_{1}^-,\ldots, \xi_{n}^-))=f(\rho(\xi_{1}^+)\ldots,\rho(\xi_{n}^+), \rho(\xi_{1}^-),\ldots, \rho(\xi_{n}^-))=f(c_1,\ldots,c_n,d_1,\ldots, d_n).$$
Since $c_1,\ldots,c_n,d_1,\ldots,d_n$ are arbitrary elements of $A$, $f(x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-)$ is a $(W,*)$-identity of $A$. Consequently, $\ker\psi=\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(A)\cap W\langle x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-\rangle$.

label: lem: upper bound
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: upper bound}
 		Let $A$ be a finite dimensional $(W,*)$-algebra over an algebraically
 		closed field $F$, where $W$ is a unital $F$-algebra. Then there exist constants $C$, $u$ such that
 		$$
 		c_n^{W,*}(A)\leq Cn^ud^n,
 		$$
 		where $d$ is the maximal dimension of a admissible $*$-subalgebra of $A$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the $(W,*)$-homomorphism $\psi\colon W\langle x_1^+, \ldots, x_n^+,x_1^-,\ldots , x_n^-\rangle \to H$ of the proposition above. Then $\psi(P_n^{W,*})\cong P_n^{W,*}(A)$, and therefore, to estimate $c_n^{W,*}(A)$, it suffices to obtain an upper bound for $\dim_F \psi(P_n^{W,*}).$ To this end, for each $0\leq r \leq n$, set $\mathcal{P}_{r,n-r}:=\psi (P_{r,n-r})$, that is, the vector space of multilinear $(W,*)$-polynomials in the variables $\xi_1^+, \ldots, \xi_r^+, \xi_{r+1}^-, \ldots, \xi_n^-$. We begin by determining an upper bound for $\dim_F \mathcal{P}_{r,n-r}$.

       Consider a monomial $w_{i_0}\xi_{\sigma(1)}^{\epsilon_{\sigma(1)}} w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_{n-1}} \xi_{\sigma(n)}^{\epsilon_{\sigma(n)}}w_{i_n}\in \mathcal{P}_{r,n-r} $, where $\sigma\in S_n$, $w_{i_l}\in \mathcal{B}_W$ for $1\leq l \leq n$, $\epsilon_i=+$ for $1\leq i \leq r$, and $\epsilon_i=-$ for $r+1\leq i \leq n$.
       Using \eqref{eq: generic elem}, such a monomial can be expressed as a linear combination of products of $n$ elements from the fixed basis $\mathcal{B}_A=\mathcal{B}^+\cup\mathcal{B}^-$ of $A$ with coefficients that are polynomials in the variables $\xi_{ij}$. More precisely, when expanded with respect to the basis $\mathcal{B}_A$, it is a linear combination of elements of the form $c\otimes \xi_{1,j_1} \cdots \xi_{n,j_{n}}$, where $c\in \mathcal{B}_A.$ Thus, we will estimate $\dim_F \mathcal{P}_{r,n-r}$ through an estimate of the number of possible monomials $\xi_{1,j_1} \cdots \xi_{n,j_{n}}$ of this last type which can appear as coefficients of $w_{i_0}\xi_{\sigma(1)}^{\epsilon_{\sigma(1)}} w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_{n-1}} \xi_{\sigma(n)}^{\epsilon_{\sigma(n)}}w_{i_n}$.

       Since $F$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, by Theorem \ref{th: WM for W*A} we write $A=B_1\oplus \cdots \oplus B_m+J$, where $J$ is the Jacobson radical of $A$ and each $B_i$ is a simple $*$-algebra satisfying $WB_l,B_lW \subseteq B_l+J$ for $1\leq l \leq m$. We may further assume that the chosen basis $\mathcal{B}_A=\mathcal{B}^+\cup\mathcal{B}^-$ of $A$ is adapted to this decomposition, in the sense that both $\mathcal{B}^+$ and $\mathcal{B}^-$ consist of elements drawn from $J$ and of each of the $B_i$.
       Since each commutative variable $\xi_{i,j}$ in \eqref{eq: generic elem} is attached to an element of either $\mathcal{B}^+$ or $\mathcal{B}^-$, by a slight abuse of terminology, we therefore refer to $\xi_{i,j}$ as a symmetric radical, skew-symmetric radical, symmetric semisimple, or skew-symmetric semisimple variable.



       Take a monomial $ \xi_{1,j_1} \cdots \xi_{n,j_{n}}$ of degree $n$ that contains $i_1$ symmetric radical variables and $i_2$ skew-symmetric radical variables. Since $J$ is a nilpotent $(W,*)$-ideal of $A$, such a monomial is nonzero only if $i_1+i_2\leq u$, where $u$ is such that $J^u\neq 0$ and $J^{u+1}= 0$. 
       Now each such monomial involves $r-i_1$ symmetric semisimple variables and $n-r-i_2$ skew-symmetric semisimple variables which come from some distinct $*$-simple components $B_{l_1}, \ldots, B_{l_p}.$ Since $W B_l, B_l W\subseteq B_l+J$, there exist distinct indices $q_1, \ldots, q_v \in \{l_1,\ldots, l_p\}$, with $1\leq v\leq p$ such that $D:=B_{q_1}\oplus \cdots \oplus B_{q_v}$ is an admissible $*$-subalgebra of $A$.

       Now, fix an admissible $*$-subalgebra $D$ of $A$. 
 	 	We recall that each monomial has $r$ coefficients taken in the set $\{\xi_{ij} \, : \, 1 \leq i \leq r, 1\leq j \leq t\}$ and $n-r$ taken in the set $\{\xi_{ij} \, : \, r+1 \leq i \leq n, 1 \leq j \leq s\}$ and also the number of possible distributions of $i_1\leq r$ symmetric radical variables and $i_2\leq n-r$ skew-symmetric radical variables in a non-zero monomial is at most $\binom{r}{i_1}\binom{n-r}{i_2}(\dim_F J)^{i_1+i_2}\leq C_1 n^u$, where $C_1$ is a constant. So, the number of possible monomials with symmetric and skew-symmetric semisimple variables coming from $D$ is bounded by $C_2n^u(\dim D^+)^r(\dim D^-)^{n-r}.$

        Now, let $M$ be the number of maximal admissible $*$-subalgebras of $A$ and let $E$ be an admissible $*$-subalgebra of maximum dimension. Then, an upper bound for the number of possible nonzero monomials is
 	 	$MC_2n^u(\dim E^+)^r(\dim E^-)^{n-r}.$
 	 	Since we rewrote any product of $n$ basis elements of $A$ as a linear combination of basis elements, we get that
$$
 	 	\dim_F \mathcal{P}_{r,n-r}\leq C_3n^u(\dim_F E^+)^r(\dim_F E^-)^{n-r},
 	 	$$
 	 	with $C_3$ constant. Since, by Proposition \ref{pro: relatively free algebra}, $\mathcal{P}_{r,n-r}\cong P_{r,n-r}(A)$, we have that $\dim_F \mathcal{P}_{r,n-r}=c_{r,n-r}(A).$ Thus, if $d=\dim_F E^+ + \dim_F E^-=\dim_F E,$ by \eqref{eq: decomp codim} we obtain
    $$
    c_n^{W,*}(A)= \sum_{r=0}^n\binom{n}{r}\dim_F \mathcal{P}_{r,n-r} \leq  C_3n^u \sum_{r=0}^n\binom{n}{r}(\dim_F E^+)^r(\dim_F E^-)^{n-r}=C_3n^ud^n,
 	$$ 	
    as required.

label: th: w*exp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th: w*exp}
 	Let $A$ be a finite dimensional $(W,*)$-algebra over a field $F$ of characteristic zero, where $W$ is a unital algebra with involution. Then the $(W,*)$-exponent $\exp^{W,*}(A)$ of $A$ exists and is equal to $*$-exponent $\exp^*(A)$ of $A$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As in the ordinary case, a careful adaptation of the proof of \cite[Theorem 4.1.9]{GiaZai} shows that the codimensions remain unchanged under extension of the base field $F$, since $F$ is infinite.
             Then by Lemmas~\ref{lem: lower bound} and~\ref{lem: upper bound} there exist constants $C_1,C_2,t_1,t_2$ such that $C_1 \geq 0$ and
$$
C_1n^{t_1}d^n \leq c_n^{W,*}(A) \leq C_2n^{t_2}d^n,
$$
where $d$ is the maximal dimension of an admissible $*$-subalgebra of $A$. Thus, the $(W,*)$-exponent $\exp^{W,*}(A)$ of $A$ exists and is equal to $d$. Moreover, by \cite[Theorem~5]{Gordienko2013}, we also have $\exp^*(A)=d$, completing the proof.

title: Corollary

label: Lem: consequence x_1^- x_2^-
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Lem: consequence x_1^- x_2^-}
        For any $k\geq 0$ we have $x_{k+1}^- x_1^+ \cdots x_k^+ x_{k+2}^-\in \langle x_1^- x_2^-\rangle_{T_W^*}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $k=0$, there is nothing to prove, so assume $k\geq 1$. We proceed by induction on $k$.

    First observe that $x_1^+ x_2^- + x_2^- x_1^+\in W\langle X, *\rangle^-$.
    Then for the base case $k=1$,
        substituting $x_1^-$ with  $x_1^+ x_2^- + x_2^- x_1^+$ in the $(W,*)$-polynomial $x_1^-x_2^-$, and then renaming the variables, yields $x_1^+ x_2^-x_3^- + x_2^- x_1^+x_3^-\in \langle x_1^- x_2^-\rangle_{T_W^*}$. Hence $x_2^- x_1^+x_3^-\in \langle x_1^- x_2^-\rangle_{T_W^*}$.

        Now assume inductively that $x_{k}^- x_1^+ \cdots x_{k-1}^+ x_{k+1}^-\in \langle x_1^- x_2^-\rangle_{T_W^*}$. Replacing $x_k^-$ with  $x_k^+ x_{k+2}^- + x_{k+2}^- x_k^+$ in this $(W,*)$-polynomial and renaming variables, we obtain
        $x_{k+1}^- x_1^+ \cdots x_{k-1}^+ x_{k+2}^- x_k^+ + x_{k+1}^- x_1^+ \cdots x_k^+ x_{k+2}^-\in \langle x_1^- x_2^-\rangle_{T_W^*}$. Consequently, by the inductive hypothesis,  $x_{k+1}^- x_1^+ \cdots x_k^+ x_{k+2}^-\in \langle x_1^- x_2^-\rangle_{T_W^*}$.

label: thm: id e cn M^D
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: id e cn M^D}
        Let $M^D$ be a $(W,*)$-algebra $M$ where $W$ acts on it as the algebra $D$ by left and right multiplication.
   Then there exists a basis $\mathcal{B}_W=\mathcal{B}_{W^+}\cup \mathcal{B}_{W^-}$  of $W$, where $\mathcal{B}_{W^+}:=\{1_W, \, w_i^+\, : \, i\geq 1\}$ and  $\mathcal{B}_{W^-}:=\{w_i^-\, : \, i\geq 1\}$ are basis of $W^+$ and $W^-$, respectively, such that  
 the $T_W^*$-ideal $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)$  of generalized $*$-identities of $M^D$ is generated, as  $T_W^*$-ideal, by the following $(W,*)$-polynomials:
        $$
        x_1^-x_2^-, 	\quad w_1^+x^-+x^-w_1^+, \quad (w_1^+)^2 x^\epsilon - x^\epsilon,
            \quad  w_i^+x^\epsilon, \quad w_j^-x^\epsilon,
        $$
        where $\epsilon\in \{+,-\}$, $i\geq 2$ and $j\geq 1$.
        Moreover  $c_n^{W,*}(M^D)=n2^{n+1}+2$.

title: Proof

label: thm: id e cn M^F
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: id e cn M^F}
    Let $M^F$ be a $(W,*)$-algebra $M$ where $W$ acts on it as the algebra $F$ by left and right multiplication.
     Then there exists a basis $\mathcal{B}_W=\mathcal{B}_{W^+}\cup \mathcal{B}_{W^-}$  of $W$, where $\mathcal{B}_{W^+}:=\{1_W, \, w_i^+\, : \, i\geq 1\}$ and  $\mathcal{B}_{W^-}:=\{w_i^-\, : \, i\geq 1\}$ are bases of $W^+$ and $W^-$, respectively, such that 
   the $T_W^*$-ideal $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^F)$  of generalized $*$-identities of $M^F$ is generated, as  $T_W^*$-ideal, by the following polynomials: 
        $$
       x_1^-x_2^-, \quad w_i^\eta x^\epsilon,
        $$
        where $\epsilon,\eta\in \{+,-\}$ and  $i\geq 1$. Moreover $c_n^{W,*}(M^F)= (n-1)2^{n}+2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Phi$ denote the acting homomorphism of $W$ on $M^F$. Then $\Phi(W)\cong F$ and we can choose a basis $\mathcal{B}_W=\mathcal{B}_{W^+}\cup \mathcal{B}_{W^-}$  of $W=W^+\oplus W^-$, where $\mathcal{B}_{W^+}:=\{ w_i^+\, : \, i\geq 0\}$ and  $\mathcal{B}_{W^-}:=\{w_i^-\, : \, i\geq 1\}$ are bases of $W^+$ and $W^-$, respectively,  such that $w_0^+=1_W$, and 
 $ w_i^+,w_i^-\in \ker \Phi$ for all $ i \geq 1.$ 
      Clearly, the $(W,*)$-identities of $M^F$ correspond to the ordinary $*$-identities of $M$ modulo the $T_W^*$-ideal $\langle w_i^{\eta} x^\epsilon   :  \epsilon,\eta\in \{+,-\}, \, i\geq 1\rangle_{T_W^*}$. Thus by \cite[Theorem 2]{MisVal} we obtain the required conclusion:
      $$\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^F)=\langle x_1^-x_2^-, \, w_i^{\eta} x^\epsilon : \epsilon,\eta\in \{+,-\}, \, i\geq 1\rangle_{T_W^*}.
      $$

      Moreover, by Lemma~\ref{Lem: consequence x_1^- x_2^-} and arguing along the same lines as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm: id e cn M^D}, with the necessary changes, we obtain the following.

      The $(W,*)$-polynomials
     \begin{equation*}
  x_{i_1}^+\cdots x_{i_{m}}^+[x_{k}^+,x_{j_1}^+,\ldots, x_{j_{n-m-1}}^+],
\end{equation*}
where $0\leq m \leq n$, $m\neq n-1$, $i_1 < \cdots < i_m$, $k>j_1< \cdots < j_{n-m-1}$, and the $(W,*)$-polynomials
  \begin{equation*}
        x_{i_1}^+\cdots x_{i_{k}}^+x_{n}^-x_{j_{1}}^+ \cdots x_{j_{n-k-1}}^+,
    \end{equation*}
     where $0\leq k \leq n-1$, $i_1< \cdots < i_k$, $j_1< \cdots < j_{n-k-1}$, form a basis of $P_{r,n-r}$ modulo $P_{r,n-r}\cap \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^F)$ for $r=n$ and  $r=n-1$, respectively. Moreover, $P_{r,n-r}\equiv 0  \pmod{(P_{r,n-r}\cap \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^F))}$ for $0\leq r \leq n-2$. Consequently, a direct counting argument yields
$$c_{r,n-r}(M^F)=\begin{cases}
(n-2)2^{n-1} +2,  & \mbox{ if } r=n, \\
2^{n-1},  & \mbox{ if } r=n-1, \\
0, & \mbox{ if } 0\leq r\leq n-2.
\end{cases}$$
Finally, by Formula~\eqref{eq: decomp codim}, we conclude that $c_n^{W,*}(M^F)= (n-1)2^{n}+2$, which completes the proof.

label: cor: mf md distinct
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor: mf md distinct}
    The $(W,*)$-algebras $M^F$ and $M^D$ generates two distinct $(W,*)$-varieties.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Given an acting $*$-homomorphism $\Phi_D$  of $W$ on $M$ such that $\Phi_D(W)\cong D$,
    by Theorem \ref{thm: id e cn M^D}  there exists a symmetric element  $w_1^+$ of $W$ linearly independent with $1_W$ such that $(w_1^+)^2x^+-x^+\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^{\Phi_D})$.
    For any acting $*$-homomorphism $\Phi_F$  of $W$ on $M$ such that $\Phi_F(W)\cong F$, we have that $\Phi_F(w_1^+)=(0,0)\in \mathcal{M}(M)$.  As a consequence, $(w_1^+)^2x^+-x^+\notin \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^F)$; indeed, $(w_1^+)^2 1_M - 1_M=-1_M\neq 0$. Therefore, $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^{\Phi_D})\not\subset \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^{\Phi_F})$ for any acting
$*$-homomorphisms $\Phi_D$ and $\Phi_F$ of $W$ on $M$ with
$\Phi_D(W)\cong D$ and $\Phi_F(W)\cong F$, and consequentially $M^F\notin \operatorname{var}^{W,*}(M^D).$
  

Now, given an acting $*$-homomorphism $\Phi_F$  of $W$ on $M$ such that $\Phi_F(W)\cong F$,
 by Theorem \ref{thm: id e cn M^F} for any element $w$ of $W$ linearly independent with $1_W$  we have that $wx^+\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^{\Phi_F})$.
 For any acting $*$-homomorphism $\Phi_D$  of $W$ on $M$ such that $\Phi_D(W)\cong D$, there exists a symmetric element  $w_1^+$ of $W$ linearly independent with $1_W$ such that $\Phi_D(w_1^+)=(R_{e_{11}+e_{44}-e_{22}-e_{33}},L_{e_{11}+e_{44}-e_{22}-e_{33}})\in \mathcal{M}(M)$. As a consequence, $w_1^+x^+\notin \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^{\Phi_D})$ since $w_1^+1_M=e_{11}+e_{44}-e_{22}-e_{33}\neq 0 $. Thus, $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^{\Phi_D})\not\subset \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^{\Phi_F})$ for any acting
$*$-homomorphisms $\Phi_D$ and $\Phi_F$ of $W$ on $M$ with
$\Phi_D(W)\cong D$ and $\Phi_F(W)\cong F$, and as a consequence $M^D\notin \operatorname{var}^{W,*}(M^F).$

label: eq: d_(p+q,p)
title: Proof
body_md:
Notice that, as a consequence of formula \eqref{eq: codim and ch M^D}, it suffices to prove that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $m_{(p+q,p),(1)}\geq 2(q+1)$ for all $p \geq 1$ and $q \geq 0$ such that $2p+q=n-1$;
    \vspace{1mm}
    \item $m_{(n-1),(1)}\geq 2n$.
\end{enumerate}
Indeed,
assume that $m_{(n-1),(1)}\geq 2n$ and $m_{(p+q,p),(1)}\geq 2(q+1)$ for all $p \geq 1$ and $q \geq 0$ such that $2p+q=n-1$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq: c_{n-1,1}(M^D) diseq}
    c_{n-1,1}(M^D)\geq\sum_{\substack{1\leq p \leq \lfloor \frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\\0 \leq q \leq n-2p-1}} 2(q+1) d_{(p+q,p)} d_{(1)}+2n d_{(n-1)}d_{(1)}.
\end{equation}
Now, by the formula $(4.8)$ proved in Theorem 4.4 of \cite{MarRiz2}, we have
\begin{equation*}\label{eq: d_(p+q,p)}
    \sum_{\substack{1\leq p \leq \lfloor \frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\\0 \leq q \leq n-2p-1}} 2(q+1) d_{(p+q,p)}=2  (2^{n-1}-n)=2^n-2n.
\end{equation*}
Hence, recalling that $d_{(n-1)}=d_{(1)}=1$, we get
$$\sum_{\substack{1\leq p \leq \lfloor \frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\\0 \leq q \leq n-2p-1}} 2(q+1) d_{(p+q,p)} d_{(1)}+2n  d_{(n-1)}d_{(1)}=2^n-2n+2n=2^n.$$
Since by \eqref{eq: c_{n-1,1}(M^D)} $c_{n-1,1}(M^D)=2^n$, it follows that \eqref{eq: c_{n-1,1}(M^D) diseq} is actually an equality. Thus the lemma follows once $(1)$ and $(2)$ are proved. 

\vspace{1ex}
We compute the two different cases separately.


       \vspace{1ex} 
\noindent\textbf{Case 1:} We prove that $m_{(p+q,p),(1)}\geq 2(q+1)$ for all $p \geq 1$, $q \geq 0$ such that $2p+q=n-1$.
		
		For $0\leq i \leq q$, we consider the following two tableaux:
         $$
			T_{(p+q,p)}^{(i)}=	\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline
				i+1 & i+2 & \dots & i+p & 1 & \dots & i & i+2p+2 & \dots & n\\ \hline
				i+p+2 & i+p+3 & \dots & i+2p+1\\ \cline{1-4}
			\end{array}
        $$
     $$   T_{(1)}^{(i)}=\begin{tabular}{|c|}
\hline
$i+p+1$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}$$
and the associated polynomials
		\begin{align}
        & a_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)=(x_1^+)^i\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p}x^-\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p}(x_1^+)^{q-i},\label{eq: a}\\
        & a_{p,q, w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)=(x_1^+)^i\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p}x^-\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p}(x_1^+)^{q-i}w_1^+,\label{eq: aw_1}
		\end{align}
		where the symbol $\tilde{\phantom{a}}$ or $\overline{\phantom{a}}$ means alternation on the corresponding variables. These generalized $*$-polynomials are obtained 
        from the quasi-idempotents corresponding to the pair of tableaux $\Big(T_{(p+q,p)}^{(i)},T_{(1)}^{(i)} \Big)$ by identifying all the elements in each row of $(p+q,p)$.
        



It is easily checked that $ a_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)$ and  $ a_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)$, for all $0\leq i \leq q$, are not $(W,*)$-identities of $M^D$. We will prove that they are linearly independent modulo $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)$. 
		
Suppose that
        $$
        \sum_{i=0}^q \alpha_i a_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)+\sum_{i=0}^q \beta_i  a_{p,q, w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)\equiv 0 \pmod{ \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)}.
        $$
        
        If we evaluate $x_1^+=k(e_{11}+e_{44})+e_{22}+e_{33}$,  $x_2^+=e_{11}+e_{44}$ and $x^-=e_{12}-e_{34}$, with $k\in F$, $k \neq 0$, we get
$$
  (-1)^p \left(\sum_{i=0}^q (\alpha_i-\beta_i) k^i \right) e_{12}
        - \left( \sum_{i=0}^q (\alpha_i + \beta_i) k^{q-i} \right) e_{34} =0.
$$
Hence, setting $t=q-i$, it follows that
$$
\sum_{i=0}^q (\alpha_i-\beta_i) k^i=0, \quad \quad  \sum_{t=0}^q (\alpha_{q-t} + \beta_{q-t}) k^{t}=0.
$$
 Now, for $0\leq i \leq q$, let $\gamma_i^{(1)}:=\alpha_i-\beta_i$ and $\gamma_i^{(2)}:=\alpha_{q-i}+\beta_{q-i}$. Given $j\in \{1,2\}$, assume that there exists $\gamma_i^{(j)}\neq 0$ for some $0\leq i \leq q $.  Since $F$ is an infinite field, we can choose $k_0,\dots,k_{q}\in F$ such that $k_i\neq 0$ and $k_i\neq k_j$ for $0\leq i \neq j \leq q$. Then, we get the following homogeneous linear system of $q+1$ equations in the $q+1$ variables $\gamma_0^{(j)}, \ldots, \gamma_q^{(j)}$
     $$
        \sum_{i=0}^{q}k_s^i \gamma_i^{(j)}=0 \quad \quad 0 \leq s \leq q.
    $$
Since the matrix associated to the above system is a Vandermonde matrix, it follows that $\gamma_i^{(j)}=0$ for any $0 \leq i \leq q$, a contradiction. Hence, for all $0\leq i \leq q$,  $\alpha_i-\beta_i=\alpha_i+\beta_i=0$ and so $\alpha_i=\beta_i=0$.

Thus the $2(q+1)$ generalized $*$-polynomials $a_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)$, $ a_{p,q, w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)$, $0\leq i \leq q$, are linearly independent modulo $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)$.
   


        
        
       
		
		Notice that for every $0\leq i \leq q$, the complete linearization of $a_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)$ and $ a_{p,q, w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+,x^-)$ are, respectively, the $(W,*)$-polynomials
        $$e_{T_{(p+q,p)}^{(i)}}e_{T_{(1)}^{(i)}}(x_1^+ \cdots x_{i+p}^+ x^-_{i+p+1} x_{i+p+2}^+ \cdots x_{n}^+ ) \quad \text{and} \quad e_{T_{(p+q,p)}^{(i)}}e_{T_{(1)}^{(i)}}(x_1^+ \cdots x_{i+p}^+ x^-_{i+p+1} x_{i+p+2}^+ \cdots x_{n}^+ w_1^+),$$ 
        which are consequently linearly independent modulo $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)$.
      Hence,  it follows that the multilinear $(W,*)$-polynomials $$e_{(p+q,p),(1)}^{(i)}(x_1^+,\ldots,x_{n-1}^+,x^-_n)\quad \text{and} \quad  e_{(p+q,p),(1)}^{(i),w_1^+}(x_1^+,\ldots,x_{n-1}^+,x^-_n),$$ 
      obtained, respectively, from the expressions above by renaming the variables, are also linearly independent modulo $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)$, for $0\leq i \leq q$, and they generate $2(q+1)$ distinct copies of the same irreducible module associated to the pair of partitions $\big((p+q,p),(1)\big)$ in the module decomposition of $P_{n-1,1}(M^D)$. So, we have that $m_{(p+q,p),(1)}\geq 2(q+1)$, as claimed.


        
\vspace{1ex}
        
\noindent\textbf{Case 2:}  We prove that $m_{(n-1),(1)}\geq 2n$.

For $0\leq i\leq n-1$ given the tableaux
$$
T_{(n-1)}^{(i)}=\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline
1   & \dots & i & i+2 & \dots & n\\  
\hline
\end{array}
$$
and
$$
T_{(1)}^{(i)}=\begin{array}{|c|}\hline
i+1\\  
\hline
\end{array}\,,
$$
the associated polynomials are respectively
\begin{align}
    b^{(i)}(x^+,x^-)&=(x^+)^ix^-(x^+)^{n-i-1} ,\label{eq: b_i} \\
      b_{w_1^+}^{(i)}(x^+,x^-)&=(x^+)^ix^-(x^+)^{n-i-1}w_1^+.\label{eq: b_{w_1i}}
\end{align}
These polynomials are obtained from the quasi-idempotents corresponding to the pair of tableaux $\left(T_{(n-1)}, T_{(1)}\right)$ by identifying all the elements in $T_{(n-1)}$.

 We will prove that the $2n$ $(W,*)$-polynomials $b^{(i)}(x^+,x^-)$, $ b_{w_1^+}^{(i)}(x^+,x^-)$, $0\leq i \leq n-1$, which are not $(W,*)$-identities of $M^D$, are linearly independent modulo $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)$. 
 
 Let
$$
 \sum_{0 \leq i \leq n-1} \alpha_i b^{(i)}(x^+,x^-)+ \sum_{0 \leq i \leq n-1} \beta_i b_{w_1^+}^{(i)} (x^+,x^-)\equiv 0 \pmod{ \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)}.
$$

By  evaluating  $x^+=k(e_{11}+e_{44})+(e_{22}+e_{33})$, $x^-=e_{12}-e_{34}$, where $k \in F$, $k\neq 0$ we get 
$$
     \left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(\alpha_i-\beta_i ) k^i\right)e_{12}-\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(\alpha_i+\beta_i)k^{n-i-1}\right)e_{34}=0.
      $$
Hence, setting $t=n-i-1$, it follows
$$
\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(\alpha_i-\beta_i ) k^i=0, \quad \quad \sum_{t=0}^{n-1}(\alpha_{n-1-t}+\beta_{n-1-t})k^{t}=0.
$$
Now, from the same argument of the previous case, we obtain $\alpha_i=\beta_i=0$ for all $0\leq i \leq n-1$. Consequently, the $(W,*)$-polynomials $b^{(i)}(x^+,x^-)$ and $b_{w_1^+}^{(i)}(x^+,x^-)$, for $0\leq i \leq n-1$, are linearly independent modulo $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)$. Applying a similar reasoning as in Case 1, this implies that $m_{(n-1),(1)} \ge 2n$, as claimed.

body_md:
By Lemma \ref{lemma: M,N-M}, there exist constants $K\leq N$ such that
    $$
    (x_1^+)^{K}x_2^-(x_1^+)^{N-K}+\hat{\alpha}(x_1^+)^Kx_2^-(x_1^+)^{N-K} w_1^++\sum_{i<K} \hat{\beta}_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^-(x_1^+)^{N-i} + \sum_{i< K}  \hat{\gamma}_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^-(x_1^+)^{N-i} w_1^+ \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}),
    $$
    where $\hat{\alpha},\hat{\beta}_i, \hat{\gamma}_i\in F$.
    Since $[x_1^+,w_1^+]$ is skew-symmetric and $x_1^-x_2^-\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)\subset \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}) $, we can move $w_1^+$ and obtain
    \begin{equation}\label{eq: id K, N-K}
        (x_1^+)^{K}(x_2^-+\hat{\alpha}x_2^-w_1^+)(x_1^+)^{N-K}+\sum_{i<K} (x_1^+)^i(\hat{\beta}_ix_2^-+\hat{\gamma}_ix_2^-w_1^+)(x_1^+)^{N-i} \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}).
    \end{equation}

First, observe that we may assume, without loss of generality, that $N=2K$ in \eqref{eq: id K, N-K}. Indeed, if $N>2K$, we multiply \eqref{eq: id K, N-K} on the left by  $(x_1^+)^{N-2K}$, thereby reducing to the case $N=2K$. Similarly, if $N<2k$,  we multiply \eqref{eq: id K, N-K} on the right by $(x_1^+)^{2K-N}$, and again we reduce to the case $N=2K$. Then,  \eqref{eq: id K, N-K} can be written as
    $$
    f:=(x_1^+)^{K}(x_2^-+\hat{\alpha}x_2^-w_1^+)(x_1^+)^{K}+\sum_{i<K} (x_1^+)^i(\hat{\beta}_ix_2^-+\hat{\gamma}_ix_2^-w_1^+)(x_1^+)^{2K-i} \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}).
    $$
    Since $f^*\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})$ and $(x_2^-w_1^+)^*- x_2^-w_1^+\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)\subset \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})$, we have
    $$
    g:=(x_1^+)^{K}(-x_2^-+\hat{\alpha}x_2^-w_1^+)(x_1^+)^{K}+\sum_{i<K} (x_1^+)^i(-\hat{\beta}_{2K-i}x_2^-+\hat{\gamma}_{2K-i}x_2^-w_1^+)(x_1^+)^{2K-i} \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}).
    $$
    Therefore,
    $$
    f-g=2(x_1^+)^{K}x_2^-(x_1^+)^{K}+\sum_{i<K} (x_1^+)^i((\hat{\beta}_i+ \hat{\beta}_{2K-i})x_2^-+(\hat{\gamma}_i-\hat{\gamma}_{2K-i})x_2^-w_1^+)(x_1^+)^{2K-i}\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}).
    $$
    As a consequence, we obtain
    $$(x_1^+)^{K}x_2^-(x_1^+)^{K}+\sum_{i<K} \beta'_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^-(x_1^+)^{2K-i}+\sum_{i<K} \gamma'_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^-(x_1^+)^{2K-i}w_1^+\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}),
    $$
   where $\beta'_i=2^{-1}(\hat{\beta}_i+ \hat{\beta}_{2K-i})$ and $\gamma'_i=2^{-1}(\hat{\gamma}_i-\hat{\gamma}_{2K-i})$. Now, if we substitute $x_2^-$ by $[x_1^+,x_2^+]$, we obtain
$$(x_1^+)^{K+1}x_2^+(x_1^+)^{K}+\sum_{i<K+1} \beta''_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^+(x_1^+)^{2K+1-i}+\sum_{i<K+1} \gamma''_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^+(x_1^+)^{2K+1-i}w_1^+\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}),
    $$
for some $\beta''_i, \gamma''_i\in F$.
 Hence, if we set $K'=K+1$ and $N'=2K+1$, then it follows that  
$$(x_1^+)^{K'}x_2^{\epsilon}(x_1^+)^{N'-K'}+\sum_{i<K'} \delta_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^{\epsilon}(x_1^+)^{N'-i}+\sum_{i<K'} \eta_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^{\epsilon}(x_1^+)^{N'-i}w_1^+\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}),
    $$
 for some $\delta_i, \eta_i\in F$, where $\epsilon\in\{+,-\}$, as desired.

label: eq: N-M
title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma \ref{lem: subvariety identity}, there exists a constant $N'$ such that
    \begin{equation}\label{eq: N-M}     (x_1^+)^{K'}x_2^{\epsilon}(x_1^+)^{N'-K'}+\sum_{i<K'} \delta_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^{\epsilon}(x_1^+)^{N'-i}+\sum_{i<K'} \eta_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^{\epsilon}(x_1^+)^{N'-i}w_1^+\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}),
\end{equation}
for some $\delta_i, \eta_i \in F$ and a suitable $K'\leq N'$, where $\epsilon\in\{+,-\}$. We will prove that $m_{\lambda, \mu}^{\mathcal{U}}\leq 4N'$  for any $(\lambda,\mu)\vdash(r,n-r)$, $0\leq r \leq n$, $n\geq 1$.

By Theorem \ref{th: cocharacter}, we only have to consider the following cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item for $r=n$,
$$
(\lambda,\mu)=
\begin{cases}
        ((p+q,p), \emptyset)\\
        ((p+q,p,1),\emptyset)\\
        ((n),\emptyset)
    \end{cases};
$$

\vspace{1mm}

\item for $r=n-1$,
$$
(\lambda,\mu)=\begin{cases}
             ((p+q,p),(1))\\
              ((n-1),(1))\\
    \end{cases}.
$$
\end{itemize}
We proceed with the same reasoning as in \cite[Proposition 5.6]{MarRiz} and \cite[Theorem 3]{MisVal}.

We prove the statement for $\lambda=(p+q,p)$ and $\mu=\emptyset$. The other cases will follow with similar arguments.
If $q \leq  N'-1 $,  then by Theorem \ref{th: cocharacter} we have $m_{\lambda,\mu}^{\mathcal{U}}\leq 4N'$, as desired. So, let us assume that $q\geq N'$ and consider $(W,*)$-polynomials  $f_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)$, $f_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)$, $g_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)$ and $g_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)$, $0\leq  i\leq q$, defined in \eqref{eq: f}, \eqref{eq: fw_1}, \eqref{eq: gi} and \eqref{eq: gw_1}, respectively, of Lemma \ref{lemma: cn,0}. 
Since
$\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p-1}[x_1^+,x_2^+]\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p-1}$ is a symmetric or a skew-symmetric element according as $p$ is even or odd, respectively, from relation \eqref{eq: N-M} it follows that
\begin{equation*}\label{eq: f polinomi}
    \begin{split}
(x_1^+)^{K'}\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p-1}[x_1^+,x_2^+]\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p-1}(x_1^+)^{N'-K'}\equiv & 
\sum_{i<K'} \delta'_i (x_1^+)^{i}\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p-1}[x_1^+,x_2^+]\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p-1}(x_1^+)^{N'-i}  \\
&+\sum_{i < K'} \eta'_i(x_1^+)^i\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p-1}[x_1^+,x_2^+]\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p-1}(x_1^+)^{N'-i}w_1^+  \pmod{\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})},
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
and by acting on the right by $w_1^+$,
\begin{equation*}\label{eq: f polinomi2}
    \begin{split}
(x_1^+)^{K'}\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p-1}[x_1^+,x_2^+]\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p-1}(x_1^+)^{N'-K'}w_1^+\equiv & 
\sum_{i<K'}\delta'_i (x_1^+)^{i}\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p-1}[x_1^+,x_2^+]\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p-1}(x_1^+)^{N'-i}w_1^+  \\
&+\sum_{i< K'} \eta'_i(x_1^+)^i\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p-1}[x_1^+,x_2^+]\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p-1}(x_1^+)^{N'-i} \pmod{\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})},
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
where  $\delta'_i, \eta'_i\in F$.
Hence, since $q\geq N'$, we can apply Relation \eqref{eq: N-M} to any polynomials $f_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)$ and $f_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)$ such that $i\geq K'$ and, as a consequence, we get
$$
f_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)\equiv \sum_{j<K'} \delta'_j f_{p,q}^{(j)}(x_1^+,x_2^+) + \sum_{j< K'} \eta'_j f_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(j)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)  \pmod{\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})}
$$
and
$$
f_{p,q, w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)\equiv \sum_{j<K'} \delta'_j f_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(j)}(x_1^+,x_2^+) + \sum_{j< K'} \eta'_j f_{p,q}^{(j)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)  \pmod{\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})}.
$$
Similarly, since the polynomial $\underbrace{\overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_1^+}}_{p-1}\left(x_1^+w_1^+x_2^+-x_2^+w_1^+x_1^+\right)\underbrace{\overline{x_2^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_2^+}}_{p-1}$ is symmetric when $p$ is even and skew-symmetric when $p$ is odd and $q\geq N'$, the relation \eqref{eq: N-M} can be applied to the polynomials $g_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)$ and $g_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)$ for every $i\geq K'$. Consequently,
$$
g_{p,q}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)\equiv \sum_{j<K'} \delta'_j g_{p,q}^{(j)}(x_1^+,x_2^+) + \sum_{j< K'} \eta'_j g_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(j)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)  \pmod{\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})}
$$
and 
$$
g_{p,q, w_1^+}^{(i)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)\equiv \sum_{j<K'} \delta'_j g_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(j)}(x_1^+,x_2^+) + \sum_{j< K'} \eta'_j g_{p,q}^{(j)}(x_1^+,x_2^+)  \pmod{\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})}.
$$
 Therefore, it follows that $m_{\lambda,\mu}^{\mathcal{U}}\leq 4K' \leq  4N'$, as desired.

label: eq: x- id
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{U}$ be a proper subvariety of $\mathcal{V}=\operatorname{var}^{W,*}(M^D)$. We shall prove that $\mathcal{U}$ has polynomial growth of the $(W,*)$-codimensions. By Lemma \ref{lem: subvariety identity}, there exist constants $K'\leq N'$ such that
    \begin{equation*}
         (x_1^+)^{K'}x_2^-(x_1^+)^{N'-K'}+\sum_{i<K'} \delta_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^-(x_1^+)^{N'-i}+\sum_{i<K'} \eta_i(x_1^+)^ix_2^-(x_1^+)^{N'-i}w_1^+\in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}),
    \end{equation*}
    for some $\delta_i, \eta_i\in F$. By substituting $x_2^-$ with $x_{N'+1}^-$ and applying the standard multilinearization process (see \cite[Theorem 1.3.8]{GiaZai}), we get
\begin{align*}
       \sum_{\sigma \in S_{N'}}x_{\sigma(1)}^+\cdots x_{\sigma(K')}^+x_{N'+1}^-x_{\sigma(K'+1)}^+\cdots x_{\sigma(N')}^+
        +\sum_{i<K'}\sum_{\sigma \in S_{N'}} \delta_i x_{\sigma(1)}^+\cdots x_{\sigma(i)}^+x_{N'+1}^-x_{\sigma(i+1)}^+\cdots x_{\sigma(N')}^+ &\\
       +\sum_{i<K'}\sum_{\sigma \in S_{N'}}\eta_i x_{\sigma(1)}^+\cdots x_{\sigma(i)}^+x_{N'+1}^-x_{\sigma(i+1)}^+\cdots x_{\sigma(N')}^+ w_1^+ & \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}).
    \end{align*}
Now, we multiply on the right by $y_1^+ \cdots y_{K'}^+$ where $y_i^+$ are new symmetric variables, and alternate $x_i^+$ with $y_i^+$ for all $1\leq i \leq K'$.  Since $[x_1^+,w_1^+]$ is skew-symmetric,
    $x_1^- x_2^- \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)\subset\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})$ and by Lemma \ref{Lem: consequence x_1^- x_2^-}, we can move $w_1^+$ to the right of any monomial in which it appears. Moreover, 
    by Lemma \ref{Lem: consequence x_1^- x_2^-} (see \cite[Remark 2]{MisVal}), any symmetric variables to the right (and to the left) of $x_{N'+1}^-$ can be reordered modulo $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(M^D)\subset\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})$. Hence, we get
    $$
     \overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_{K'}^+}x_{N'+1}^-\overline{y_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{y_{K'}^+}{x_{K'+1}^+}\cdots {x_{N'}^+}\ \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}).
    $$
    If we multiply on the left by $y_{K'+1}^+\cdots y_{N'}^+$ and we alternate $x_j^+$ with $y_j^+$ for all $K'+1\leq j\leq N'$, we obtain
 \begin{equation}\label{eq: x- id}
     \overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_{N'}^+}x_{N'+1}^-\overline{y_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{y_{N'}^+}\ \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}),
 \end{equation}
 and by acting on the left by $w_1^+$ we get
  \begin{equation}\label{eq: x- id w_1}
     \overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_{N'}^+}x_{N'+1}^-\overline{y_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{y_{N'}^+}w_1^+\ \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}).
 \end{equation}
This proves that, for all $q\geq 0$ and $0\leq i\leq q$, the $(W,*)$-polynomials $a_{p,q}^{(i)}$ and $a_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(i)}$, defined in \eqref{eq: a} and \eqref{eq: aw_1}, respectively, in Lemma~\ref{lemma: cn-1,1}, belong to $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})$ whenever $p\geq N'$. Consequently, $m_{(q+p,p),(1)}^{\mathcal{U}}=0$ when $p\geq N'$.
 



    Since $z_1^+w_1^+z_2^+-z_2^+w_1^+z_1^+$ is skew-symmetric,  if we substitute  $x_{N'+1}^-$ in \eqref{eq: x- id} and \eqref{eq: x- id w_1} with $[z_1^+,z_2^+]$ or with $z_1^+w_1^+z_2^+-z_2^+w_1^+z_1^+$, where $z_i^+$ are new symmetric variables, we obtain
$$
         \overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_{N'}^+}[z_1^+,z_2^+]\overline{y_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{y_{N'}^+},\quad \overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_{N'}^+}[z_1^+,z_2^+]\overline{y_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{y_{N'}^+}w_1^+\ \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}),
         $$
    and
    $$
         \overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_{N'}^+}(z_1^+w_1^+z_2^+-z_2^+w_1^+z_1^+)\overline{y_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{y_{N'}^+},\quad \overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_{N'}^+}(z_1^+w_1^+z_2^+-z_2^+w_1^+z_1^+)\overline{y_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{y_{N'}^+}w_1^+\ \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}).
$$
As above, for all $q\geq 0$ and $0\leq i\leq q$, the $(W,*)$-polynomials $f_{p,q}^{(i)}$, $f_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(i)}$, $g_{p,q}^{(i)}$, and $g_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(i)}$, defined in \eqref{eq: f}--\eqref{eq: gw_1}, respectively, in Lemma~\ref{lemma: cn,0}, belong to $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})$ whenever $p\geq N'+1$. Consequently, $m_{(q+p,p),\emptyset}^{\mathcal{U}}=0$ when $p\geq N'+1$.

    If we substitute $x_{N'+1}^-$ in \eqref{eq: x- id} and \eqref{eq: x- id w_1}  with $\widehat{z_1^+}\widehat{z_2^+}\widehat{z_3^+}$, where $z_i^+$ are new symmetric variables, we obtain 
$$
 \overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_{N'}^+}\widehat{z_1^+}\widehat{z_2^+}\widehat{z_3^+}\overline{y_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{y_{N'}^+},\quad \overline{x_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{x_{N'}^+}\widehat{z_1^+}\widehat{z_2^+}\widehat{z_3^+}\overline{y_1^+}\cdots \widetilde{y_{N'}^+}w_1^+\ \in \operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U}).$$
Thus, as in the previous cases, for all $q\geq 0$ and $0\leq i\leq q$, the $(W,*)$-polynomials $h^{(i)}_{p,q}$ and $h_{p,q,w_1^+}^{(i)}$, defined in \eqref{eq: h} and \eqref{eq: hw_1}, respectively, in Lemma~\ref{lemma: cn,0}, belong to $\operatorname{Id}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})$ whenever $p\geq N'+1$. Consequently, $m_{(q+p,p,1),\emptyset}^{\mathcal{U}}=0$ when $p\geq N'+1$.


Finally, since $\mathcal{U}$ is a subvariety of $\operatorname{var}^{W,*}(M^D)$, by Theorem \ref{th: cocharacter} we have that $m_{\lambda,\mu}^{\mathcal{U}}=0$ for all $(\lambda,\mu)\vdash (r,n-r)$ and $0\leq r \leq n-2$.

In conclusion, by Theorem \ref{th: cocharacter} in all cases we have proved that $m_{\lambda,\mu}^{\mathcal{U}}=0$ for all $\lambda$ with more than $N'+2$ boxes below the first row
or, equivalently, if $\chi_\lambda \otimes \chi_\mu$ appears with a non-zero multiplicity in the generalized $S_r\times S_{n-r}$-cocharacter of $\mathcal U$, then $\lambda$ must contain at most $N'+1$ boxes below the first row. As a consequence, for $0\leq r \leq n$ and $n\geq 0$ we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq: chi U}
      \chi_{r,n-r}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})=\sum_{\substack{(\lambda,\mu)\vdash (r,n-r)\\
    r-\lambda_1\leq N'+1\\
    n-r\leq 1}}m_{\lambda, \mu}^{\mathcal{U}}(\chi_{\lambda} \otimes \chi_{\mu}),
\end{equation}
    where $\lambda_1$ stands for the number of boxes of the first row of $\lambda.$


    Since $r-\lambda_1\leq N'+1$, then $\lambda_1\geq r-(N'+1)$. By the hook formula 
    $$
    d_{\lambda}=\chi_{\lambda}(1)\leq \frac{r!}{(r-(N'+1))!}\leq r^{N'+1}\leq n^{N'+1}.
    $$ 
   Also recall that $d_{\mu}=\chi_{\mu}(1)=1$ whenever $\mu=\emptyset$ or $\mu=(1)$. 
   Thus, since $c_{r,n-r}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})= \chi_{r,n-r}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})(1)$, by Formulas~\eqref{eq: decomp codim} and \eqref{eq: chi U}, and Proposition~\ref{prop: n barra}, we get
   \begin{align*}
       c_n^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})=& \sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r} \chi_{r,n-r}^{W,*}(\mathcal{U})(1)= \sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r} \sum_{\substack{(\lambda,\mu)\vdash (r,n-r)\\
    r-\lambda_1\leq N'+1\\
    n-r\leq 1}}m_{\lambda, \mu}^{\mathcal{U}} d_{\lambda}d_{\mu}\\
    =& \sum_{\substack{(\lambda,\mu)\vdash (n,0)\\
    n-\lambda_1\leq N'+1}}m_{\lambda, \mu}^{\mathcal{U}} d_{\lambda}d_{\mu} +n \sum_{\substack{(\lambda,\mu)\vdash (n-1,1)\\
    n-1-\lambda_1\leq N'+1}}m_{\lambda, \mu}^{\mathcal{U}} d_{\lambda}d_{\mu}\\
    \leq & \sum_{\substack{(\lambda,\mu)\vdash (n,0)\\
    n-\lambda_1\leq N'+1}}\bar{N}n^{N'+1}+n \sum_{\substack{(\lambda,\mu)\vdash (n-1,1)\\
    n-1-\lambda_1\leq N'+1}}\bar{N}n^{N'+1} \leq (N'+1)^2\bar{N}(n+1)n^{N'+1},
   \end{align*}
    since the number of partitions such that $r-\lambda_1\leq N'+1$ is bounded by $(N'+1)^2$.
    Therefore, $c^{W,*}_n(\mathcal{U})$ is polynomially bounded and $\operatorname{var}^{W,*}(M^D)$ has almost polynomial growth, as required.
